name: Motion Actuation
explanation: If a feature can be triggered by physically moving the device, like shaking a phone to undo an action, or by moving the user's body in front of a camera, it must also be operable through a regular interface control, like a button, and there must be a way to turn off the motion-based trigger to prevent it firing accidentally. Exceptions apply when the motion is processed through an accessibility-supported API designed for this purpose, or when responding to motion is essential to the activity and disabling it would defeat the feature's purpose, like a step-counter or a bubble-level app.
whoItAffects: People who can't physically shake, tilt, or move a device, due to a motor disability, or because the device is mounted in a fixed position like a wheelchair-mounted tablet, cannot trigger motion-based actions at all and need an equivalent button or control instead. People with hand tremors or involuntary movements can trigger a motion-activated feature accidentally through normal handling of the device, so a way to disable that trigger prevents unwanted actions from firing unexpectedly during ordinary use.
howToTest: Identify any feature that responds to physically moving or shaking the device, or to the user's own body movement captured by a camera. For each one, check whether the same function can also be triggered through a standard on-screen control like a button, and whether there's a setting to turn off the motion-based trigger entirely. If motion is the only way to trigger the feature, with no button alternative and no way to disable it, and the feature isn't inherently motion-dependent, like a pedometer, this fails.

check.question: A note-taking app lets users shake their phone to undo their last edit, with no on-screen undo button available and no setting to disable the shake gesture. Does this pass SC 2.5.4 Motion Actuation?
choices: Yes, because shake-to-undo is a well-known and intuitive gesture
No, because there is no button-based alternative and no way to disable the motion trigger
Yes, because undo is a secondary, non-essential feature
It depends only on how sensitive the shake detection is calibrated
